h1:
Prachinburi on a Budget
Herbs, Waterfalls & Ancient Ruins
intro: Prachinburi is a province where you get a lot without spending much. Plenty of the highlights are free or charge just a few tens of baht to enter — the Abhaibhubejhr herbal garden, the waterfalls on the Prachinburi side of Khao Yai, and some genuinely old ruins. Food starts in the tens of baht too. We've laid this out as a 2-day, 1-night plan so you can see what it actually costs and how to string the stops together without wearing yourself out.

blocks.html: Prachinburi sits only about 130 km from Bangkok — a little over two hours by car or minivan — which makes it a good fit for a weekend trip when you don't want to burn through your budget. The appeal here is that nature and history sit close together, and most of your money goes to food and a room rather than entry fees. We wrote this plan around places that are genuinely open to visit, with rough prices we found in reviews and official notices. Use it as a frame and tweak it to your own pace.

items: Several highlights are free — the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building, the herbal garden, and some of the ruins charge nothing to enter.
Waterfall fees are tiny — the falls inside the Khao Yai zone on the Prachinburi side charge around 40 THB; kids and visitors over 60 get in free.
Food starts in the tens — local boat noodles start at 20 THB a bowl at markets and shops around town.
Close to Bangkok — a little over two hours by car, so fuel and transport stay cheap; a day trip is doable too.

blocks.title: Keeping costs down
blocks.html: If you travel as a group of 3–4 and split fuel and the room, the per-person cost drops a lot. Many hotels in Prachinburi town run from the high hundreds to low thousands of baht per night. Booking ahead on a weekday is cheaper than a weekend.

blocks.title: Book the activities in your Prachinburi trip ahead
blocks.text: Booking online ahead on Klook or GetYourGuide is usually cheaper than the gate and skips the queue. Pick only the experiences you actually want — prices and availability are shown live on each site.

items.label: Day trips from Prachinburi
items.note: Out and back in a day

blocks.text: Day 1 — Herbs, history and cheap eats

blocks.html: Day one stays around town and the Si Mahosot side — easy travel, low entry fees. Start the morning at Abhaibhubejhr, then move on to the ruins.

items.activity: Leave Bangkok; grab boat noodles on the way or wait until you reach Prachinburi
items.note: Local boat noodles start at 20 THB a bowl — order several and you're still under 100.

items.activity: Visit the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building, a Victorian-style structure over a century old, now a Thai traditional medicine museum
items.note: Free entry, open Mon–Fri 08:00–16:00. Check ahead for weekends, as some sections close.

items.activity: Walk the Abhaibhubejhr herbal garden right next door, see the herb plots and photo spots, and stop by the shop for inhalers and herbal soap
items.note: Walking around is free, and the herbal souvenirs are inexpensive — easy, cheap things to take home.

items.activity: Lunch at a local spot in town — a made-to-order shop or a chemical-free vegetable restaurant doing single-plate dishes
items.note: A single-plate meal runs about 50–80 THB; ordering shared dishes works out better value.

items.activity: Drive over to Si Mahosot district to see the Sa Morakot ruins at Wat Sa Morakot, with their old twin Buddha footprint
items.note: Part of the ancient Si Mahosot city site, free to enter — walk among traces of the Dvaravati civilization.

items.activity: Stop by the Sri Maha Bodhi tree, believed to be the oldest in Thailand, near Sa Morakot
items.note: It's close by, so you can fit it into the same loop. Free entry.

items.activity: Check into your hotel in Prachinburi town, drop your bags and head out for dinner
items.note: Staying in the town area makes it easy to walk out for food.

items.activity: A budget dinner — mookata (Thai BBQ hotpot) or a made-to-order restaurant in town
items.note: Plenty of mookata buffets in town run a few hundred baht per person and fill you up well.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Khao Yai waterfalls, Prachinburi side

blocks.html: Day two heads out to nature on the Noen Hom side, the Prachinburi gateway into Khao Yai. The waterfalls here are cheap to enter and best for swimming from late rainy season into early winter, when there's plenty of water.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Waterfall dips and the drive home

items.activity: Breakfast at the hotel or a congee–patongko (Thai doughnut) shop in town
items.note: An easy breakfast runs about 30–50 THB.

items.activity: Drive up Khao Ito to Khao Ito Waterfall, a recreation forest near town — walk around and take photos
items.note: Usually no entry fee, though there may be a small maintenance or parking charge at times. Keep some cash on you.

items.activity: Continue to Takhro Waterfall in Khao Yai National Park, a wide, shallow pool that's good for getting in the water
items.note: Park entry is 40 THB per person; kids and visitors over 60 get in free. There are food stalls and shops at the entrance.

items.activity: Lunch at a restaurant near the waterfall entrance, or a som tam–grilled chicken spot around Noen Hom
items.note: Som tam, grilled chicken and sticky rice — a set for a couple hundred baht feeds several people.

items.activity: Stop at a mountain-view café around Noen Hom before heading back, for a coffee and a rest
items.note: Drinks run 50–80 THB a glass; pick a spot with mountain views from the seats.

items.activity: Set off back to Bangkok, stopping for herbal souvenirs or seasonal fruit along the way
items.note: Prachinburi is fruit country — in durian and santol season there are roadside stalls.

blocks.html: Food is the easiest part of this trip to keep in check. Prachinburi is known for boat noodles starting at 20 THB a bowl, so even ordering several won't dent your wallet. Here's the kind of low-cost food you'll find all over town.

items.name: Boat noodles
items.blurb: The town's signature dish — a rich broth you don't need to season, tender braised pork, and easy to order several bowls at once. The cheapest meal of the trip.

items.name: Som tam & grilled chicken
items.blurb: Easy to find around Noen Hom and on the way up to the waterfalls. Order a set of som tam, grilled chicken and sticky rice to share — great value for a group.

items.name: Rice & curry / made-to-order
items.blurb: Plenty of shops in town to choose from — a single plate fills you up, ideal for a quick meal or keeping costs down.

items.name: Chemical-free vegetable food
items.blurb: Prachinburi has health-food restaurants using chemical-free vegetables and no MSG — homely flavors that cost less than you'd expect.

items.name: Mookata buffet
items.blurb: The dinner where locals gather — a buffet for a few hundred baht per person, filling and good value. A solid way to cap off day one.

items.name: Seasonal fruit
items.blurb: Prachinburi is fruit country — in durian, santol and mangosteen season, roadside stalls sell it fresh and cheaper than in Bangkok.
items.meta: Seasonal · tens to hundreds of baht per kilo

blocks.title: Straight talk
blocks.html: The prices here are rough ranges from reviews and official notices; they can shift with the season and the shop. It's safest to check a shop's page or call ahead before you go, especially smaller places with unpredictable days off.
Work out the numbers for a group of 3–4 splitting fuel and the room, and you'll see this 2-day, 1-night trip easily comes in around the low thousands of baht per person.

items: Travel — driving and splitting fuel + tolls works out to about 300–500 THB/person (a minivan costs about the same).
Entry fees — under 100 THB/person for the whole trip, since many spots are free and the waterfalls charge just tens of baht.
Food — 3 main meals + snacks, about 300–500 THB/person if you stick to cheap eats.
Accommodation — a twin room split two ways is about 400–700 THB/person, depending on the hotel.
Rough total — about 1,100–1,800 THB/person for 2 days, 1 night.

items.name: Day trip, 1 day
items.blurb: Skip the room and do just the town + ruins, or just the waterfalls. Keeps the budget at a few hundred baht per person.

items.name: Full 2-day, 1-night plan
items.blurb: You get the herbs, the ruins and the waterfalls without rushing — good for a weekend, low thousands of baht.

blocks.text: When it's best value to go

items: Late rainy to early winter (around Oct–Jan) — the waterfalls are full and the weather's pleasant, good for swimming.
Fruit season (around May–Jul) — durian, santol and mangosteen are plentiful, cheap to eat and take home.
Weekdays — rooms are cheaper than weekends, and the waterfalls and ruins are quieter and easier to walk.

faq.q: How much does a budget trip to Prachinburi cost?
faq.a: A 2-day, 1-night trip focused on cheap eats and traveling as a group runs about 1,100–1,800 THB per person, covering travel, entry fees, food and the room. A single-day trip leaves you at just a few hundred baht per person, since you cut out the accommodation.

faq.q: Which Prachinburi attractions are free to enter?
faq.a: The Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building and the herbal garden are free. The Sa Morakot ruins at Wat Sa Morakot and the Sri Maha Bodhi tree charge nothing either. Khao Ito Waterfall is usually free too, with maybe a small maintenance or parking charge.

faq.q: How much do Prachinburi's waterfalls cost to enter?
faq.a: Takhro Waterfall, inside Khao Yai National Park, charges 40 THB per person; kids and visitors over 60 get in free. Khao Ito Waterfall is generally free. Fees can change, so keep some cash on you.

faq.q: What's cheap and good to eat in Prachinburi?
faq.a: Boat noodles are the signature dish, from 20 THB a bowl — order several and it's still cheap. There's also som tam with grilled chicken, rice and curry, chemical-free vegetable food, and mookata buffets for a few hundred baht per person. In fruit season there's durian and santol sold cheap by the roadside.

faq.q: What's the cheapest way to get to Prachinburi?
faq.a: It's about 130 km from Bangkok, a little over two hours by car. Traveling as a group of 3–4 and splitting fuel keeps it very cheap, or a minivan/bus from Mochit costs about the same. Distances in town are short, but the waterfalls are outside town, so a private vehicle is more convenient.
